entry.title: fix(ci): repair environment bootstrap and language-neutrality check
entry.content:
fix(ci): repair environment bootstrap and language-neutrality check

Both jobs failed on the first push, for unrelated reasons.

`uv pip install --system` refuses to install: the runner's system Python is
externally managed (PEP 668), and `uv python install` does not change which
interpreter `--system` resolves to. Create a project virtualenv and run the
tools through `uv run` instead.

The language-neutrality job flagged its own documentation. It grepped the source
for target-language words, and `core/protocols.py` says, in a comment, that the
engine folds accents "because a course asked it to, not because it knows about
Portuguese" — the rule being explained, reported as the rule being broken.

Replaced with `scripts/check_language_neutral.py`, which parses the source and
inspects identifiers and non-docstring string literals, ignoring comments and
docstrings entirely. That matches what the rule actually says: an identifier or a
default value encoding one language's behaviour is a violation; prose about the
policy is not. Verified in both directions — it passes the current engine and
catches a planted `{"vocabulario": 0.5}` and a `grade_portugues()`.

Signed-off-by: Michał Weiss <mikub97@gmail.com>

entry.title: docs: add agent working context, tuning rationale and label taxonomy
entry.content:
docs: add agent working context, tuning rationale and label taxonomy

Phase 1b of the rebuild plan: make the repository legible to an agent that has
never seen it, so a task costs three files of reading rather than thirty.

  - docs/tuning.md — every constant with the symptom it treats and, where one
    exists, the measurement that set it. Marks each as measured, reasoned or
    conventional, so it is clear which numbers are defensible and which are
    borrowed and open to being measured properly. Also records the policy
    constants still in the private predecessor, before that reasoning is lost
    in the move.
  - content/CLAUDE.md — the answer-leak rule and why it quarantines rather than
    warns: the predecessor logged a warning and 70 of 330 items leaked anyway.
  - courses/CLAUDE.md — id immutability, provenance, and why an unlicensed
    image is a repository-ending mistake rather than a tidy-up item.
  - .claude/skills/repetita-issue — turns a rough report into an issue in the
    definition-of-ready format, with a worked example of the transformation.
  - .github/labels.yml + scripts/sync-labels.sh — three state labels used as a
    queue (agent-ready / needs-spec / human-only) plus area labels.

Signed-off-by: Michał Weiss <mikub97@gmail.com>

entry.title: chore: rename project to repetita
entry.content:
chore: rename project to repetita

`roda` was the working name inherited from the private app's database
filename. It is unusable as a published name: the PyPI package is taken, Roda
is an established Ruby web framework, and RODA is a digital-preservation
repository. All three would have made the project unfindable.

`repetita` is from *repetita iuvant* — "things repeated help", which states the
premise of spaced repetition about two thousand years before anyone measured
it. The root is legible without translation across Polish, English, Portuguese,
French and Spanish, and it names the mechanism rather than any one subject: the
engine schedules cards, and cards can be Portuguese verbs or bones of the hand.

Renames the package, the CLI, the RODA_* environment variables and every
reference in the docs. No behaviour changes.

Signed-off-by: Michał Weiss <mikub97@gmail.com>

entry.title: feat: scaffold engine with core types, graders and scheduler backends
entry.content:
feat: scaffold engine with core types, graders and scheduler backends

Extracts the spaced-repetition engine from a private app (Research/hub, tab
`pt`) into a standalone MIT-licensed project. That app stays running and
untouched; nothing here reads or writes its database.

The structural change is separating three things the old design conflated in
one YAML `type:` field — what the knowledge is (note), which direction it is
tested in (card, the unit of scheduling), and how it is asked right now (form).
See ADR-0001.

Included:
  - core: Rating, Response, Judgement, and the Grader / SchedulerBackend /
    Presenter protocols. Response carries an audio channel from the start, so
    adding speaking practice later does not mean rewriting every grader.
  - graders: typed, sentence, choice, self. Accent folding, punctuation and
    sentence slack are course configuration, not engine behaviour — the engine
    contains no target language, and CI checks that.
  - srs: sm2 and leitner behind one protocol. Leitner exists to keep the
    protocol honest; a protocol with one implementation is a description of
    that implementation.
  - property tests over interval bounds, due-date monotonicity and purity.

Fixes a scheduling bug carried over from the original: HARD sat below the pass
threshold and was handled identically to AGAIN, so a missing accent erased a
45-day interval and recorded a lapse — the exact outcome the grading code's own
docstrings said must not happen. No test covered it. HARD now passes with a
reduced interval and an ease penalty. See ADR-0002.

Signed-off-by: Michał Weiss <mikub97@gmail.com>
